reference.title: Dumbbell Upright Row
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Shoulders, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you pull up, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; moderate, with the elbows stopping at about shoulder height
prescription.progression: Add reps, then weight; keep the range at or below shoulder height

cues.text: Stand tall, feet about hip width, knees soft, ribs down and glutes lightly braced. Dumbbells in front of the thighs, palms facing you, hands about shoulder width.
Breathe out and lead with the elbows: pull the dumbbells up close to the body.
Stop with the elbows at about shoulder height, above the wrists, hands at the lower chest. Do not shrug to the ears.
Lower under control in about 2 s, dumbbells close to the body.
Arms long in front of the thighs; reset and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling the elbows above shoulder height
mistakes.fix: Stop at about shoulder height: upright rows above 90 degrees of elevation were linked to impingement signs (impingement study 2014).

mistakes.mistake: Hands leading the elbows, wrists curling up
mistakes.fix: Think "elbows up and out"; the wrists stay below the elbows and roughly straight.
Stand tall with the ribs down; use a lighter weight.
Keep the hands about shoulder width (wider grips used more deltoid and trapezius, less biceps).

kinematics.norm: Stop at about 90 degrees of elevation, elbows at shoulder height; rows above 90 degrees were associated with impingement signs (impingement study 2014; Schoenfeld 2011)
Arms long at the bottom; elbows bent about 90-110 degrees at the top (clinical opinion)
Hands travel straight up close to the body, about shoulder width apart; wider grips raised deltoid and trapezius activity (grip width study 2013)
Controlled, about 1-2 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #043712, Dumbbell Upright Row, video (movement reference)
Effect of grip width on electromyographic activity during the upright row (J Strength Cond Res 2013;27(1):181-187, PubMed 22362088)
Characteristics of shoulder impingement in the recreational weight-training population (J Strength Cond Res 2014;28(4):1081-1089, PubMed 24077379)
Schoenfeld, Kolber & Haimes 2011, the upright row: implications for preventing subacromial impingement (Strength Cond J 33(5):25-28)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Keep the elbows at or below shoulder height; people with shoulder impingement may need to skip this exercise or use a lateral raise instead (Schoenfeld 2011).
modify: Pinching at the top: stop lower (elbows below shoulder height) and keep the hands a little wider.
Wrist discomfort: let the wrists stay straight and the dumbbells turn slightly.
regressions: Lighter dumbbells and a shorter range.
Dumbbell lateral raise (no internal rotation at the top).
progressions: Pause for 1 s at the top.
High pull from the hang (power variation, with coaching).

muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Lifts the elbows out and up. Deltoid activity rose with grip width in the barbell upright row (grip width study 2013); dumbbells let the hands sit about shoulder width.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Lifts the elbows out and up. Deltoid activity rose with grip width in the barbell upright row (grip width study 2013); dumbbells let the hands sit about shoulder width.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Elevates and upwardly rotates the shoulder blades as the elbows rise; trapezius activity also rose with a wider grip (grip width study 2013).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Elevates and upwardly rotates the shoulder blades as the elbows rise; trapezius activity also rose with a wider grip (grip width study 2013).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Helps lift the arm, more so if the dumbbells drift forward.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Helps lift the arm, more so if the dumbbells drift forward.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bends the elbow; a narrow grip used the biceps more and the deltoids less (grip width study 2013).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Bends the elbow; a narrow grip used the biceps more and the deltoids less (grip width study 2013).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade with the trapezius.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade with the trapezius.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Pulls the elbows out and slightly back; posterior deltoid activity differed with grip width (grip width study 2013).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Pulls the elbows out and slightly back; posterior deltoid activity differed with grip width (grip width study 2013).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: keeps the ball of the shoulder centred while the arm is turned in.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: keeps the ball of the shoulder centred while the arm is turned in.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk upright: no leaning back to swing the weights.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the spine tall against the load in front.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the spine tall against the load in front.

phases.label: Dumbbells in front of the thighs

guides.label: Straight up, close to the body
